newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends mostly down as origins sell.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends mostly down as origins sell.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were mostly lower by the close as origin selling took centrestage after the market bounced higher in the morning, traders said.
"There was a feeling that the market would go higher this week because people feel the market was a bit oversold," said one.
"We saw that but origin selling came in and it got knocked down. It (the selling) got a little bit too much."
The morning business was also marked by trade short-covering and profit-taking.
But traders noted that New York arabica futures shot up after the London market had closed. "This shows that London was holding it back," the trader said.
By the close, January was $7 down at $1,304 a tonne while March gave up $6 at $1,233.
Both positions hit session lows of $1,301 and $1,231 respectively and traders said there was good at support at around $1,300 and $1,230.
Volume was 6,199 lots, with the bulk of the trades centred on January and March contracts.
There were no fresh fundamental inputs driving the market but traders said the major factor in the coming months is the size of the 1997/98 Brazilian coffee crop.
So far, preliminary estimates have varied widely from below 20 million 60-kg bags to as high at 32 million and compared with 26-28 million this season.
Some Brazilian agronomists have put the coming crop at below 20 million bags although a more reliable assessment is not likely to emerge until the end of January.
But traders said based on previous years, Brazil's own projections had proved to be accurate.
Although the Brazilians might talk the market up, "one should bear in mind that their track record hasn't been too bad over the last couple of seasons", said one.
In other news, Vietnam's state coffee firm Vinacafe denied reports that beans from the country's main producing area of Dak Lak were being hit by mould problems.
